lesson.summary: Understand patterns are designed for collaboration from first principles, with a small runnable example.

stage.name: Pattern Principles

stage.description: What patterns are, how to describe them, and the principle of favouring composition over inheritance.

chapter.title: What Are Design Patterns? Why Use Them?

payload.markdown: By their nature, patterns should be generative and composable. This means that you should be able to apply one pattern and thereby create conditions suitable for the application of another. In other words, in using a pattern, you may find other doors opened for you. Pattern catalogs are usually designed with this kind of collaboration in mind, and the potential for pattern composition is always documented in the pattern itself.

items: Composition: Building classes from other objects instead of inheriting from them.
Conditions: Branching a program with if, elseif, else and match.
Behavioral Patterns: Patterns that distribute responsibility and coordinate behaviour.
Creational Patterns: Patterns that control how objects come into being.
Enterprise Patterns: Patterns for service layers, domain objects and application architecture.
Error Patterns: Repeatable strategies: fail fast, wrap and rethrow, aggregate and report.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
Pattern Principles: What design patterns are, how to describe them, and when one fits.
